newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore trade in covering for RSS1 and TSR20.
newsitem.headline: Singapore trade in covering for RSS1 and TSR20.

text.p: Trading in the Singapore rubber market closed on Thursday with shortcovering seen for RSS3 and TSR20 grade rubber, dealers said.
"There was some shortcovering by European rubber houses for RSS3 and TSR20 rubber," a trader said.
There was no impact in the market from news that the Thai government bought 14,800 tonnes of RSS3 rubber at 109 U.S. cents a kg, traders said.
"It had no real impact in the market because people still believe that the fundamentals are bearish and consumer demand is weak," another dealer said.
The trade was keeping an eye on the strike by 13,000 workers in Goodyear Tire and the possible sale in the U.S. next week by the Defense Logistics Agency (DLA) of some amounts of rubber, they said.
"People are waiting here for the DLA sales and waiting to see what the impact of that would be," a dealer said.

At around 0945 GMT, July RSS3 was seen at 107.00 U.S. cents a kg from 107.25 cents. July RSS1 was seen at 155.75 Singapore cents (US$1.08) a kg from 155.50 cents. July TSR20 was seen at 149.00 Singapore cents (US$1.03) a kg from 148.50 cents.
